item.title: Minimum wage hikes take effect for 880,000 workers across the U.S.
item.description: Many workers in the U.S. are seeing pay increases this week as new minimum wage laws take effect in states like Alaska, California, Oregon, and Washington, D.C., along with cities including Chicago and Los Angeles. While the federal minimum wage has remained unchanged at $7.25 since 2009, local governments are stepping up to provide necessary raises amid rising living costs. item.title: UK’s Largest Solar Park Enters Commercial Operation
item.description: Quinbrook Infrastructure Partners has announced that the Cleve Hill Solar Park in the UK, boasting a capacity of 373 MW, is now operational. This facility, which combines solar power and energy storage, is the largest of its kind in the UK, marking a significant milestone in renewable energy development. For more details, visit the full article at POWER Magazine. This article was sourced, curated, and summarized by MindLab

item.title: U.S. Arrests Key Facilitator in North Korean IT Worker Scheme, Seizes $7.74 Million
item.description: The U.S. Department of Justice has launched a major crackdown on North Korean IT workers, resulting in one arrest and the seizure of numerous financial accounts, fraudulent websites, and nearly 200 computers. This coordinated effort involved searching 21 suspected "laptop farms" across 14 states, highlighting the ongoing battle against illicit North Korean cyber activities. This article was sourced, curated, and summarized by MindLab

item.title: US Vape Market Reels Under Tariff Pressure
item.description: In June, the FDA revealed a dramatic decline in vape shipments from China, with only 71 recorded between May 1-28, down from almost 1,200 in previous periods. This significant reduction raises questions about the impact of regulatory changes and market dynamics on the vaping industry.
